spec: The launchability question's world knowledge, in two blocks (issues #36, #66 and #776). 'systems' records formats that are real content for a platform and still launch nothing until an installation step has run: the *distribution form* of the content itself (a PSN package is the only form many digital-only PS3 titles exist in), which an emulator installs rather than starts. Keyed by the atlas system id and the exact extension token ES-DE would derive (case-sensitive, leading dot); consulted before any entry is asked, whatever the system's accept-list says, since the record is about the platform's format and the question is the emulator's (issue #776). Each record names its 'installers' (issue #717): the emulators that install the format, each by the token ES-DE's own commands spell it with (the X of %EMULATOR_X%), cited in the record's source. An empty list is a statement, not a gap: the format still has to be installed, and no emulator RetroDECK or EmuDeck sets up installs it. 'emulators' records what a STANDALONE launch entry's own loader reads — the per-entry half of the same question, keyed by the %EMULATOR_…% token the way every standalone card family is. A standalone emulator is its own gate: unlike a libretro entry, whose claims are read live off the installed core and whose archives RetroArch opens for it, a standalone opens the file itself and refuses what its loader does not know. 'accepts' are extension tokens matched case-insensitively (the gate is the emulator's loader, not ES-DE's case-exact scan), 'archives' whether the loader opens archive containers at all — where it does, an archive the card takes answers launchable with archive-contents-unread, since what loads is inside it (issue #744). An emulator absent from this block is one whose loader nobody has read: the verdict is 'unestablished', never a refusal — the same discipline the mods table spells out for its absences. 'directories' (issue #776) states what the loader does with a directory it is handed, read at the card's build: 'recognises' are the names inside a directory the loader starts one by, in the order it tests them, and an empty list says it starts no directory at all; 'source' cites it. A card may state four things more, three since issue #618 and one since issue #744. 'arguments' are the argument lists it was read for: the words a command hands the emulator after its token, %ROM% among them, so an entry whose command hands it anything else is one the card does not answer for and stays unestablished; a card without the key answers for every command naming its token. Words in front of the token leave the arguments as they are where they only set what runs the emulator — a leading 'env NAME=value…', and ES-DE's %INJECT% of a per-game file, whose text ES-DE places where the word stood (FileData.cpp:1672-1791 @ v3.4.1) and which is not read here. 'content_checked' true says the loader goes on to read the file's content once the extension has passed, which this table does not read: an accepted extension answers launchable with that stated. 'build_dependent' names the extensions the builds the card serves disagree on, each with the citation naming them: such an extension answers unestablished, because a refusal would not hold on every machine the card serves. 'build' (issue #744) is the revision the card was read at, one of the builds the emulator's save card pins in standalone_saves.json: the stamp that holds the pin against the deployed binary stays there, in one place, and a test fails where a card names a revision its save card does not pin, or, where the emulator is deployed, one other than the revision of the build whose stamp the deployed binary carries. Schema 2 added 'installers', schema 3 those three card keys, schema 4 'build', schema 5 'directories'.

directories.source: [D] Azahar 3e574df8: GetLoader opens the path as a file and identifies it by its bytes, then by its extension (src/core/loader/loader.cpp:150-183, IdentifyFile :20-36), and System::Load fails where no loader follows (src/core/core.cpp:308-318). A directory yields no bytes to identify, so nothing in that route starts one.

AZAHAR.source: [D] The shipped azahar binary's own load surface (RetroDECK 0.10.9b, components/azahar/bin/azahar): the dialog filters '3DS ROM Files (*.cia *.cci *.3dsx *.cxi *.3ds)' and '3DS Compressed ROM Files (*.zcia *zcci *z3dsx *zcxi)' are whole literals — the latter three spelled without their dot upstream, a glob that still matches the dotted names, recorded here in the dotted form a file yields. Those two filters are the compress and decompress dialogs' (GMainWindow::OnCompressFile, src/citra_qt/citra_qt.cpp:3302, and OnDecompressFile, :3395, @ 3e574df8), not the boot path's, and two of their tokens are not loaded (issue #717, [V] at the same revision): booting a .cia only asks 'CIA must be installed before usage' and offers to install it, launching nothing (citra_qt.cpp:1481-1490); a .zcia is typed a CIA by its extension (src/core/loader/loader.cpp:63-64) and GetFileLoader holds no loader for that type (:145-146), so the boot finds none; and the game list's boot set carries neither (GameList::supported_file_extensions, src/citra_qt/game_list.cpp:1121-1125). Every token kept is one that set carries. Both formats are recorded as install-first under n3ds instead. archives=false is the unfiltered scan's negative: the only strings containing 'zip' are gzip fragments (no archive loader), and the load error literal 'the selected file is not a compatible 3DS ROM format or is encrypted' names the gate a wrong format hits. The kept tokens rest on that scan, hence [D]; issue #66 carries the case that founded this (a zipped 3DS ROM handed to Azahar starts a process that loads nothing).

directories.source: [V] Dolphin f84df020: BootParameters::GenerateFromFile takes a path by its extension, cut at the last dot and folded (Source/Core/Core/Boot/Boot.cpp:206-215), and opens it as a disc or an executable file (:246-270); any other path is 'Could not recognize file' (:308). An extracted disc boots through its sys/main.dol file, which the blob reader recognises by that file's path (Source/Core/DiscIO/DirectoryBlob.cpp:256-259), never through the directory itself. Release 2606a (c77bbaa0), the build EmuDeck installs from Flathub, does the same (Boot.cpp:201-210, :241-264, :303 there).

DOLPHIN.source: [V] Dolphin f84df020 (release 2609, the build RetroDECK ships and the Dolphin save card pins). -e (--exec, Source/Core/UICommon/CommandLineParse.cpp:87-91) names the file, -b (--batch, :114-116) runs without the interface, and DolphinQt hands the file to BootParameters::GenerateFromFile (Source/Core/DolphinQt/Main.cpp:219-226). That cuts the extension at the last dot (SplitPath, Source/Core/Common/StringUtil.cpp:323-356) and folds its ASCII case (ToLower, :909-912, through the classic locale, StringUtil.h:308-311) before anything else (Source/Core/Core/Boot/Boot.cpp:212-215). A .m3u or .m3u8 is read as a list whose first entry takes its place (:217-228); the disc set .gcm .bin .iso .tgc .wbfs .ciso .gcz .wia .rvz .nfs .dol .elf is opened as a disc (CreateDiscForCore, :243-253), where a .dol or .elf that holds none boots as an executable (:255-267) and any other file of the set is refused (:269-270); a .dff is a FIFO log (:273-274), a .wad a WAD (:276-281) and a .json a game-mod descriptor that boots its base file (:283-306). Every other extension is refused, 'Could not recognize file' (:308-309): no branch takes an archive. Past the extension each branch reads the content — the disc's container by its magic (CreateBlobReader, Source/Core/DiscIO/Blob.cpp:213-252) and the Wii or GameCube magic at 0x18 or 0x1C (TryCreateDisc, Source/Core/DiscIO/Volume.cpp:111-129), a WAD's header (TryCreateWAD, :151-164), the list's entries, the descriptor — hence content_checked. EmuDeck installs Dolphin from Flathub (functions/EmuScripts/emuDeckDolphin.sh:5, :39 at EmuDeck backend 863ab69d), a build that moves with Flathub; release 2606a (c77bbaa0) takes the same extensions (Boot.cpp:191-303 there).

directories.source: [V] RetroDECK/Duckstation 1f6de046b: the start checks that the file exists with FileSystem::FileExists (src/duckstation-qt/qthost.cpp:2476-2482), which answers false for a directory (src/common/file_system.cpp:2465-2474), so a directory ends the start 'does not exist'. stenzek/duckstation 2dd5cc3c, the build EmuDeck installs, checks the same way (src/duckstation-qt/qthost.cpp:3505-3510; src/common/file_system.cpp:2846-2855 there).

build_dependent..ccd: RetroDECK/Duckstation 1f6de046b, the build RetroDECK ships, answers a .ccd 'Unknown extension' (CDImage::Open, src/util/cd_image.cpp:116); stenzek/duckstation, whose newest release EmuDeck installs (getReleaseURLGH, functions/helperFunctions.sh:415-448, called from functions/EmuScripts/emuDeckDuckStation.sh:15 at EmuDeck backend 863ab69d: the first x64 AppImage of the repository's releases, prereleases included), opens it (src/util/cd_image.cpp:101-104 at 2dd5cc3c, the tag preview as of 2026-11-03).
build_dependent..cpe: RetroDECK/Duckstation 1f6de046b, the build RetroDECK ships, boots no .cpe as an executable (IsExeFileName, src/core/system.cpp:777-781) and its CDImage::Open answers it 'Unknown extension' (src/util/cd_image.cpp:116); stenzek/duckstation, whose newest release EmuDeck installs (getReleaseURLGH, functions/helperFunctions.sh:415-448, called from functions/EmuScripts/emuDeckDuckStation.sh:15 at EmuDeck backend 863ab69d), boots it as one (IsExePath, src/core/system.cpp:669-673 at 2dd5cc3c, the tag preview as of 2026-11-03).
build_dependent..elf: RetroDECK/Duckstation 1f6de046b, the build RetroDECK ships, boots no .elf as an executable (IsExeFileName, src/core/system.cpp:777-781) and its CDImage::Open answers it 'Unknown extension' (src/util/cd_image.cpp:116); stenzek/duckstation, whose newest release EmuDeck installs (getReleaseURLGH, functions/helperFunctions.sh:415-448, called from functions/EmuScripts/emuDeckDuckStation.sh:15 at EmuDeck backend 863ab69d), boots it as one (IsExePath, src/core/system.cpp:669-673 at 2dd5cc3c, the tag preview as of 2026-11-03).

DUCKSTATION.source: [V] RetroDECK/Duckstation 1f6de046b (the build RetroDECK ships and the DuckStation save card pins). -batch only sets batch mode (src/duckstation-qt/qthost.cpp:2337) and the other words are the file (:2461-2463), which must exist (:2476-2482) before System::BootSystem takes it. That compares the end of the whole path without case, before any disc is opened: .exe .psexe .ps-exe .psx boot as an executable (IsExeFileName, src/core/system.cpp:777-781, :1601-1605) and .psf .minipsf as a PSF (IsPsfFileName, :783-786, :1606-1610); every other file goes to CDImage::Open (:1625), whose failure ends the boot. CDImage::Open cuts the suffix at the path's last dot (strrchr, src/util/cd_image.cpp:64) and compares it without case (Strcasecmp): .cue :81, .bin .img .iso :85-86, .chd :90, .ecm :94, .mds :98, .pbp :102 and .m3u :106 are opened, and every other extension is refused, 'Unknown extension' (:114-117) — .ccd .toc .mdf .cbn .z .znx .7z .zip among them: no branch opens an archive, and a launched .mdf is refused even though the .mds beside it opens it. A .cue, .bin, .img, .iso, .mds or .m3u is judged by what DuckStation opens through it (atlas.disc_opens, issue #716), which answers before this card is asked. Past the extension each branch reads the content — a CHD's header and tracks, the ECM magic, the PBP's header, PARAM.SFO and disc images (encrypted ones refused), and for an executable or a PSF the file's own header, loaded at the BIOS's kernel-init hook, where a failed load shuts the started system down (Bus::KernelInitializedHook, src/core/bus.cpp:1012-1041) — hence content_checked. stenzek/duckstation, whose newest release EmuDeck installs, takes three extensions more: see build_dependent. Its GPU dump replays (.psxgpu, and .psxgpu.zst or .psxgpu.xz; IsGPUDumpPath, src/core/system.cpp:681-685 at 2dd5cc3c) are refused here, since a replay starts no game on any build.

directories.source: [V] PCSX2 v2.8.2 = fd9d310c: VMManager::AutoDetectSource requires FileSystem::FileExists (pcsx2/VMManager.cpp:1240-1247), which answers false for a directory (common/FileSystem.cpp:2368-2380), so a directory ends the start 'does not exist'. v2.9.152 = da6bae10, the newest release EmuDeck installs, does the same (pcsx2/VMManager.cpp:1266-1270; common/FileSystem.cpp:2368-2380 there).

PCSX2.source: [V] PCSX2 v2.8.2 = fd9d310c (the build RetroDECK ships and the PCSX2 save card pins). -batch only sets batch mode (pcsx2-qt/QtHost.cpp:2200-2203), a word starting with '-' that names no option ends the start (:2331-2335), and the other words are the file (:2341-2344), booted with no extension check (:2550-2551). VMManager::AutoDetectSource compares the end of the whole path without case: a GS dump (.gs .gs.xz .gs.zst, :1250-1253, IsGSDumpFileName :2432-2436) replays one, a .elf (:1255-1270, IsElfFileName :2422-2425) is handed to the emulated BIOS, and every other file is opened as a disc image (:1275-1278). The image's reader is picked by the extension after its last dot, compared without case (GetFileReader, pcsx2/CDVD/InputIsoFile.cpp:40-57; Path::GetExtension, common/FileSystem.cpp:576-583): .chd, .cso or .zso, .gz and .dump have readers of their own, and every other extension is read as a flat image (:56) — .iso .bin .img .mdf .nrg, and the .ngr the ps2 list spells beside .NRG. Detect then refuses an image of under 17 sectors, 'Unable to identify the ISO image type' (:205, :282-283), which fails the start (VMManager.cpp:1456-1463), and takes any larger file in which it finds no disc as an audio CD (InputIsoFile.cpp:272-313), so the BIOS boots with no game. That is why the card refuses what PCSX2 never reads as a game: a .zip, .7z, .ciso or .isz goes to the flat reader unopened, and no disc is found in it; a .cue or .m3u is read as a flat image too, a list of under 17 sectors, so the start fails, and so is the .desktop shortcut the ps2 list carries for ES-DE's shortcut entry; a GS dump replay starts no game either. Past the extension each reader reads the content — the CSO or ZSO magic (CsoFileReader.cpp:36-62), the block dump signature (BlockdumpFileReader.cpp:38-42), the gzip stream and its index, the CHD through libchdr with a parent looked for in its own directory (ChdFileReader.cpp:239, :345-346), a flat image's sectors — and a .elf is loaded by the emulated BIOS, which keeps running where the load fails; hence content_checked. EmuDeck installs the newest release of PCSX2/pcsx2, prereleases included (getReleaseURLGH, functions/helperFunctions.sh:415-448, called from functions/EmuScripts/emuDeckPCSX2QT.sh:19 at EmuDeck backend 863ab69d); v2.9.152 = da6bae10, the newest as of 2026-11-03, picks the source and the reader the same way (VMManager.cpp:1272-1299, InputIsoFile.cpp:40-57, :282, :306 there).

directories.source: [V] PPSSPP v1.20.4 = fa50bb19: Identify_File takes a directory holding EBOOT.PBP as a PBP directory and one holding PSP_GAME as a disc directory, in that order (Core/Loaders.cpp:87-98); the first boots the EBOOT.PBP inside (ResolveFileLoaderTarget, :283-291; Core/System.cpp:330-331) and the second is mounted as the disc (:295-297). Any other directory is refused, 'Just a directory.' or 'This is save data, not a game.' (:236-238). The Flathub build EmuDeck installs builds this same commit.

PPSSPP.source: [V] PPSSPP v1.20.4 = fa50bb19 (the build RetroDECK ships and the PPSSPP save card pins). The first word that is no option is the file, which must exist, and a second one ends the start (UI/NativeApp.cpp:600-657). Identify_File decides by the file's bytes (Core/Loaders.cpp:68-281), with the extension cut at the last dot and lowercased (GetExtFromString, Common/File/Path.cpp:165-180): a disc image's container and its volume descriptor (:125-199, where a PS1, PS2 or PS3 image or one that is no PSP game is refused), then the first four bytes — a ZIP, a PBP, a 7z, an ELF (:203-263), where an ELF is a PSP ELF only under .elf .prx .pbp .plf or no extension (:224-231) and a PS1 eboot is refused, 'PS1 EBOOTs are not supported by PPSSPP.' (Core/System.cpp:239) — and the extension only as a fallback where no magic matched (:264-280). So .chd .cso .iso .pbp .elf .prx are taken and their bytes decide, which atlas does not read: hence content_checked. A 7z archive is identified by its magic and never booted, '7z file detected (Require 7-Zip)' (Loaders.cpp:220-221, System.cpp:232); only a misnamed file would boot, so the card refuses .7z. A ZIP is opened by the loader itself (ResolveFileLoaderTarget, Loaders.cpp:283-321): the first .iso, .cso or .chd at most one folder deep is booted from inside it (DetectZipFileContents, :473-641, :536-546), and a ZIP holding none fails the boot, 'ZIP file detected (Require UnRAR)' (System.cpp:226-228) — inside the archive, which atlas does not read: hence archives. EmuDeck installs the Flathub build org.ppsspp.PPSSPP (functions/EmuScripts/emuDeckPPSSPP.sh:5, :17 at EmuDeck backend 863ab69d), which builds this same commit (org.ppsspp.PPSSPP.yml:70-73 at flathub/org.ppsspp.PPSSPP@8dadba9d).

directories.source: [V] PrimeHack 81bfb96: Dolphin's loader as of that fork — GenerateFromFile takes a path by its extension (Source/Core/Core/Boot/Boot.cpp:197-206) and opens it as a disc or an executable file (:236-260); any other path is 'Could not recognize file' (:298). 53f53e0f, the Flathub build, does the same (:201-209, :264, :303 there). A directory is no disc or executable file.

build_dependent..bin: PrimeHack 81bfb96, the build RetroDECK ships, leaves .bin out of its disc set (Source/Core/Core/Boot/Boot.cpp:234-235), so such a file is refused, 'Could not recognize file' (:298-299); 53f53e0f, the build the io.github.shiiion.primehack manifest on Flathub names (io.github.shiiion.primehack.yml:76-78 at flathub/io.github.shiiion.primehack@06ae9d6b) and so the one EmuDeck installs (functions/EmuScripts/emuDeckPrimehack.sh:6, :19 at EmuDeck backend 863ab69d), carries it in that set (Boot.cpp:238-240 there).

PRIMEHACK.source: [V] PrimeHack 81bfb96 (the build RetroDECK ships and the PrimeHack save card pins), Dolphin's loader as of that fork. -e (--exec, Source/Core/UICommon/CommandLineParse.cpp:88-92) names the file, -b (--batch, :115-117) runs without the interface, and DolphinQt hands the file to BootParameters::GenerateFromFile (Source/Core/DolphinQt/Main.cpp:194-201). That cuts the extension at the last dot (SplitPath, Source/Core/Common/StringUtil.cpp:304-335) and folds its ASCII case (ToLower, :679-682, through the classic locale, StringUtil.h:279-282) before anything else (Source/Core/Core/Boot/Boot.cpp:203-206). A .m3u or .m3u8 is read as a list whose first entry takes its place (:208-219); the disc set .gcm .iso .tgc .wbfs .ciso .gcz .wia .rvz .nfs .dol .elf is opened as a disc (CreateDisc, :234-243), where a .dol or .elf that holds none boots as an executable (:245-257) and any other file of the set is refused (:259-260); a .dff is a FIFO log (:263-264), a .wad a WAD (:266-271) and a .json a game-mod descriptor that boots its base file (:273-296). Every other extension is refused, 'Could not recognize file' (:298-299): no branch takes an archive. Past the extension each branch reads the content — the disc's container by its magic (CreateBlobReader, Source/Core/DiscIO/Blob.cpp:217-256) and the Wii or GameCube magic at 0x18 or 0x1C (TryCreateDisc, Source/Core/DiscIO/Volume.cpp:87-100), a WAD's header (TryCreateWAD, :112-125), the list's entries, the descriptor — hence content_checked. The disc set is where the builds part: see build_dependent.

.cia.statement: a CTR importable archive — an installer, not loadable content: the emulator installs the title it carries into its own NAND and SD trees first, and the title is then launched by its installed form
.cia.source: [V] Azahar refuses to boot a .cia: BootGame asks 'CIA must be installed before usage' and offers InstallCIA alone (src/citra_qt/citra_qt.cpp:1481-1490 @ 3e574df8); its install dialog takes '*.cia *.zcia' (OnMenuInstallCIA, :2414-2418), and the game list's boot set carries no .cia (src/citra_qt/game_list.cpp:1121-1125). AzaharPlus carries the same refusal and the same install dialog (src/citra_qt/citra_qt.cpp:2703-2712, :3643-3647 @ cf90688448). The installers are the two tokens ES-DE v3.4.1's n3ds system runs them with, %EMULATOR_AZAHAR% and %EMULATOR_AZAHARPLUS% (RetroDECK 0.10.10b declares the first and carries the second in a comment). The other standalones ES-DE declares for n3ds (Citra, Mandarine, Lime3DS, Panda3DS) are not recorded: their source was not read at a pinned revision. Neither ES-DE v3.4.1's n3ds accept-list nor RetroDECK 0.10.10b's carries .cia, so the frontend never scans one.

.zcia.statement: a compressed CTR importable archive — an installer, not loadable content: the emulator installs the title it carries first, and the title is then launched by its installed form
.zcia.source: [V] Azahar installs a .zcia through the same dialog as a .cia ('*.cia *.zcia', src/citra_qt/citra_qt.cpp:2414-2418 @ 3e574df8), decompressing it on the way in (Service::AM::InstallCIA, src/core/hle/service/am/am.cpp:1059-1073); booting one finds no loader, since the extension types it a CIA (src/core/loader/loader.cpp:63-64) and GetFileLoader has none for that type (:145-146), and the game list's boot set carries no .zcia (src/citra_qt/game_list.cpp:1121-1125). AzaharPlus's install dialog takes it the same way (src/citra_qt/citra_qt.cpp:3643-3647 @ cf90688448). Installer tokens and the standalones not recorded as for .cia. Neither ES-DE v3.4.1's n3ds accept-list nor RetroDECK 0.10.10b's carries .zcia.

.edat.statement: a PSN content license (EDAT) — installed beside the title it unlocks, never launched: RPCS3 copies it into the user's exdata folder
.edat.source: [V] RPCS3's package install takes .edat files with packages and licenses: its file dialog offers '*.pkg *.PKG *.rap *.RAP *.edat *.EDAT' (main_window::InstallPackages, rpcs3/rpcs3qt/main_window.cpp:833 @ d5213de6), and each .edat is copied into dev_hdd0/home/<user>/exdata (install_filetype, :869-904; InstallFileInExData, :778-816). The installer is the %EMULATOR_RPCS3% token every RPCS3 entry of ES-DE v3.4.1 and RetroDECK 0.10.10b runs (the ps3 system's shortcut entry runs %EMULATOR_OS-SHELL% instead). Neither accept-list carries .edat (.desktop .iso .ISO .ps3 .PS3 .ps3dir .PS3DIR).

.pkg.statement: a PSN package — an installer, not loadable content: RPCS3 installs it into its dev_hdd0 tree first, and the title is then launched by its installed form
.pkg.source: [V] RPCS3 installs packages through main_window::InstallPackages: its file dialog offers '*.pkg *.PKG *.rap *.RAP *.edat *.EDAT' (rpcs3/rpcs3qt/main_window.cpp:833 @ d5213de6), and every .pkg left once the licenses are copied goes to HandlePackageInstallation (:913-936); the command line forces the same install with --installpkg (rpcs3/rpcs3.cpp:411, :833, :1182-1185). The installer is the %EMULATOR_RPCS3% token every RPCS3 entry of ES-DE v3.4.1 and RetroDECK 0.10.10b runs (the ps3 system's shortcut entry runs %EMULATOR_OS-SHELL% instead). Neither accept-list carries .pkg (.desktop .iso .ISO .ps3 .PS3 .ps3dir .PS3DIR), so the frontend never scans one. Surfaced by decky-romm-sync#1582: a largest-file fallback picked the multi-gigabyte package and baked a command RPCS3 could not act on.

.rap.statement: a PSN license file — installed alongside its package, never launched: without the matching .pkg installed it activates nothing
.rap.source: [V] The same RPCS3 install takes .rap files (the file dialog, rpcs3/rpcs3qt/main_window.cpp:833 @ d5213de6) and copies each into dev_hdd0/home/<user>/exdata (install_filetype, :869-904; InstallFileInExData, :778-816), before any package. The installer is the %EMULATOR_RPCS3% token every RPCS3 entry of ES-DE v3.4.1 and RetroDECK 0.10.10b runs (the ps3 system's shortcut entry runs %EMULATOR_OS-SHELL% instead). Neither accept-list carries .rap.

.pkg.statement: a PS4 package — the content's distribution form, which has to be extracted before anything launches, and no emulator RetroDECK or EmuDeck sets up installs it
.pkg.source: [V] shadPS4 removed its package installer in be22674f8c ('code: Remove fpkg code', 2025-03-28), deleting its package reader (src/core/file_format/pkg.h, pkg_type.cpp), the package viewer and the install path of src/qt_gui/main_window.cpp; neither shadPS4 at ce74386 nor its Qt launcher at 811fb031 carries one since. shadPS4 is the only emulator ES-DE v3.4.1, RetroDECK 0.10.10b and EmuDeck's custom_systems overlay (backend 863ab69d) declare for ps4, and none of their ps4 accept-lists carries .pkg (.bin .BIN .desktop .ps4 .PS4, and .desktop alone on EmuDeck), so the frontend never scans one.

.pkg.statement: a PSN package for the PS Vita — an installer, not loadable content: Vita3K installs it together with its license, a zRIF string or a license file, and the title is then launched by its installed form
.pkg.source: [V] Vita3K installs a .pkg given with its zRIF on the command line (--pkg with --zrif, vita3k/config/src/config.cpp:361-363; install_pkg, vita3k/main.cpp:145-151 @ e6ac4272), and its install dialog takes one .pkg with at most one license file, a .bin or .rif (resolve_pkg_selection, vita3k/gui-qt/src/pkg_install_dialog.cpp:57-89). The installer is the %EMULATOR_VITA3K% token the psvita entry of ES-DE v3.4.1 and RetroDECK 0.10.10b runs; that entry starts an installed title by its id (-r %INJECT%=%BASENAME%.psvita), and the accept-list carries .psvita alone.

.rif.statement: a PS Vita license file — installed beside the title it unlocks, never launched
.rif.source: [V] Handed a .rif, Vita3K installs it as a license and boots nothing (is_rif, copy_license, vita3k/main.cpp:221, :238-240 @ e6ac4272); its license dialog takes '*.bin *.rif' (vita3k/gui-qt/src/license_install_dialog.cpp:59). Only the command line keys on the exact name work.bin (vita3k/main.cpp:221); the dialogs take any .bin as a license (license_install_dialog.cpp:59; is_license_file, vita3k/gui-qt/src/pkg_install_dialog.cpp:42), which a record keyed by extension cannot tell from other .bin content, so .bin is not recorded. The installer is the %EMULATOR_VITA3K% token the psvita entry of ES-DE v3.4.1 and RetroDECK 0.10.10b runs; the accept-list carries .psvita alone.

.vpk.statement: a PS Vita application archive — an installer, not loadable content: handed to Vita3K it is installed and then booted in one invocation, yet the title runs from its installed form
.vpk.source: [V] Vita3K treats a .vpk as an archive to install (is_archive, install_archive, vita3k/main.cpp:220, :226-233 @ e6ac4272) and boots the title it installed only afterwards, where the archive held a game (category gd, :229-233, :247-249). The installer is the %EMULATOR_VITA3K% token the psvita entry of ES-DE v3.4.1 and RetroDECK 0.10.10b runs; that entry starts an installed title by its id (-r %INJECT%=%BASENAME%.psvita), and the accept-list carries .psvita alone.

.zip.statement: a PS Vita content archive — an installer, not loadable content: handed to Vita3K it is installed, and booted in the same invocation where it holds a game, yet the title runs from its installed form
.zip.source: [V] Vita3K treats a .zip exactly as a .vpk: an archive to install (is_archive, install_archive, vita3k/main.cpp:220, :226-233 @ e6ac4272), booted afterwards only where it held a game (category gd, :229-233, :247-249), so a patch or an add-on is installed and nothing boots. The installer is the %EMULATOR_VITA3K% token the psvita entry of ES-DE v3.4.1 and RetroDECK 0.10.10b runs; the accept-list carries .psvita alone.
